newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weak as Nigeria profits taken.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weak as Nigeria profits taken.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended weaker on Friday as dealers booked profits made during a late session rally prompted by news of reduced production in Nigeria due to renewed communal disturbances, brokers said.

June Brent crude jumped to $18.52 a barrel, just below an early session high, in late afternoon trade on news that Shell had been forced to shut in 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Nigerian production but then fell away sharply to close only a cent off the low at $18.26, 15 cents down on the day.
"People went long on the back of the Nigeria news and then decided to take cover before the weekend," said a broker.
Confirmation from the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) that no May exports have so far been cancelled helped take some of the heat out of the rally, dealers said.
NNPC said Forcados cargoes scheduled to load from April 29 to May 6 had been put back by two days. Lifters of Forcados loading from May 7-20 had been informed of a three-day delay.
Thin volumes were also partly to blame for Brent's late slide, brokers said.
"There was a chance of a bullish close with U.S. products holding up well but the volume has just not been good enough to take us through some pretty important resistance," said one.
Earlier, IPE gas oil closed stronger in thin volume, having spent most of the day tracking crude.
May IPE gas oil last traded 75 cents higher at $165.25 a tonne, having earlier tested but failed at resistance of $167.00.
